description: Per-layout arrays of character spawn positions and rotations that override stage defaults for a mission wave.

Id.technical: FName import key/row name for FGameDataTableRow_MissionLayout. It is not chosen directly by gameplay: AGameBattleManager::GetCharacterStartTransform first finds the active Map row, indexes MapRow->Id_MissionLayout with the current MissionWave->MissionLayoutIndex, and then resolves that id against MissionLayoutDataTables (DTM+0x9B0).

Location.simple: Spawn positions, indexed by battle character slot.
Location.technical: TArray<FVector>, default empty. If Layout->Location.IsValidIndex(Index), GetCharacterStartTransform replaces the translated component of the start transform with Location[Index]. The Z component is subsequently overwritten by GameBattle_TraceGroundHeight over the world, so the authoritative final height is ground-traced rather than the raw data value. No layout row is selected when MapRow->Id_MissionLayout is out of range or None.

Rotation.simple: Spawn rotations, indexed by battle character slot.
Rotation.technical: TArray<FRotator>, default empty. If Layout->Rotation.IsValidIndex(Index), the start transform's rotation is set from FQuat(Rotation[Index]). Unlike Location, the final rotation is not ground-adjusted; when the array does not contain the slot the transform from the battle area (or identity) is kept.

notes: The exported asset contains 137 rows; its RowStruct is FGameDataTableRow_MissionLayout and the manager loads MissionLayoutDataTable into MissionLayoutDataTables (DTM+0x9B0).
Rows are reached through a cross-table join: MissionWave.MissionLayoutIndex -> Map.Id_MissionLayout[] -> MissionLayout row. This is the only consumer identified in the reconstructed source.
The spawn-transform function is reconstructed with retail RVA 0x1015dc0 in comments; the scoreboard should be consulted for its current byte/status state.
Only available C++ and the export were reviewed; not a claim about every retail or Blueprint use.

usages.detail: GetCharacterStartTransform applies Location and Rotation for the active wave's layout row.
Battle entry construction calls GetCharacterStartTransform for each character slot.
